knowledge:
- key_parameters: dist=Set to "norm" (Gaussian) or "nbinom" (negative binomial) to choose the distribution ;; phi=Optional dispersion estimate for the negative binomial distribution ;; gamma=Optional offset for the negative binomial distribution
- alternatives: edgeR=For shrinkage estimation and scale normalization to improve the negative binomial mixture model ;; PDGEtest=For non-parametric mixture testing to increase robustness against outliers
- when_to_use: When testing for association between quantitative traits (e.g., gene expression) and a grouping variable (e.g., SNPs) where one group is homogeneous (labelled, e.g., homozygous wild-type) and the other is a mixture of two classes (unlabelled, e.g., heterozygous/homozygous mutant).
- pitfalls: The null distribution of the likelihood-ratio test statistic is unknown, requiring resampling (parametric bootstrapping or permutation via scrutor). The grouping variable must be correctly binarised with the labelled group as 0 and the unlabelled group as NA.

workflows.name: semi_supervised_association_testing
workflows.intent: Fit semi-supervised mixture models and test for associations between quantitative traits and SNPs/grouping variables.
input: y (vector of quantitative trait observations) or Y (matrix of quantitative traits)
snp (vector of SNP genotypes) or SNPs (matrix of SNP genotypes)
workflows.stages: 1. Binarise the SNP/grouping variable to define labelled (0) and unlabelled (NA) groups ;; 2. Fit the mixture model to estimate parameters and predict class labels ;; 3. Perform hypothesis testing using parametric bootstrapping or permutation to calculate p-values
workflows.code:
n <- length(snp)


z <- rep(NA,times=n)
z[snp==0] <- 0

n <- nrow(SNPs)
p <- ncol(SNPs)

Z <- matrix(NA,nrow=n,ncol=p)
Z[SNPs==0] <- 0

fit <- mixtura(y,z)
class <- round(fit$posterior)
fit$estim1
fit$estim0

scrutor(y,z)
scrutor(y,Z)
scrutor(Y,z)
scrutor(Y,Z)
